stack: Backend: FastAPI (Python), SQLite (WAL mode), single uvicorn worker, systemd on one VPS
Frontend: Tauri (Rust shell) + vanilla TypeScript + Vite, no framework
AI: Anthropic (Claude) via 8 backend service files
Integrations: Google/Microsoft OAuth (email send), Companies House REST+Streaming, Apify, Mailchimp
limitations: No live browser/UI automation performed — this is a native Tauri desktop app, not a website; Phase 6's workflow evaluation was done via static code-path tracing, not timed live interaction

Direct production-database row-level queries were blocked twice by this environment's own permission classifier; the confirmed 29x DB-growth finding is based on file-size/filesystem observation (ls, df, crontab -l), not a table-level breakdown — the exact cause is Inferred, not Confirmed
No frontend lint/static-analysis tool is configured in this repo (no eslint/biome config exists), so 'existing lint results' could not be reported because none exist

Competitor research relied on live WebSearch/WebFetch; a few official pricing pages (Salesforce, Apollo, HubSpot) returned errors or JS-only shells to the fetch tool and were cross-corroborated via third-party pricing trackers instead, flagged inline in 02-competitor-benchmark.md

core_crm_completeness.weakest_aspect: Deals/Pipeline: real data model, effectively no usable UI (see visual audit orphaned-screen finding)

visual_system_and_polish.strongest_aspect: The token system's underlying design and the documented legacy-alias backward-compatibility shim
visual_system_and_polish.weakest_aspect: Type-scale bypass rate (58% of all font-size declarations are raw, one-off values)
visual_system_and_polish.path_to_60: Consolidate the font-size/padding/border-radius bypass and build one shared modal component
visual_system_and_polish.path_to_75: Standardise loading/error-state coverage across all screens to match Dashboard's reference pattern
visual_system_and_polish.path_to_90: Full accessibility pass (aria-labels, focus-visible rings) and reduced-motion support

usability_and_information_architecture.evidence: 10 of 15 declared screens are reachable; 3 fully-built screens are structurally orphaned from navigation; dead data-admin-only markup; a redundant device-local Settings PIN gate layered on top of the real permission system; sparse accessibility (5 aria-labels vs 334 interactive controls).
usability_and_information_architecture.strongest_aspect: The 10 reachable top-level sections map cleanly to real daily jobs, no evidence of nav-bloat/clutter
usability_and_information_architecture.weakest_aspect: 3 finished screens (Call Queue, Opportunity Workspace, AI Sales Intelligence) unreachable through any navigation path
usability_and_information_architecture.path_to_60: Reconnect or deliberately retire the orphaned screens; remove the dead admin-only markup and redundant PIN gate
usability_and_information_architecture.path_to_75: Add a command palette; add sub-view-level permission granularity for the Outreach sub-tools

integration_readiness.evidence: 3 integrations exist and are individually well-engineered (email OAuth with correct CSRF handling, Companies House with retry/backoff/idempotency, Anthropic with real cost controls); no connector framework, no calendar/telephony provider, no public API/webhooks, no marketplace.
integration_readiness.strongest_aspect: The Companies House streaming integration's retry/backoff/idempotency/self-pruning design
integration_readiness.weakest_aspect: No provider-neutral connector abstraction — each integration hand-built from scratch; no calling-provider or calendar-sync integration at all
integration_readiness.path_to_60: Extract the CH stream's pattern into a reusable SyncJob/SyncCursor abstraction; add Google/Outlook Calendar sync
integration_readiness.path_to_75: Add a provider-neutral calling adapter plus one named calling provider (Aircall)
integration_readiness.path_to_90: Build a real 'Connected Apps' settings surface with health/reconnect UX; add a public API + webhooks

multi_tenant_saas_readiness.evidence: Confirmed by repo-wide grep: zero references to workspace/tenant/organisation_id anywhere in the backend. Single shared users table, no org boundary on any of 33 tables. No self-serve signup, no billing/subscription/plan-gating, no email-based invites, no trial lifecycle.
multi_tenant_saas_readiness.strongest_aspect: The existing custom RBAC/permission-string model is a genuine foundation to layer org-scoping onto — it is not a rebuild, just an extension
multi_tenant_saas_readiness.weakest_aspect: No tenant/organisation concept exists anywhere in the schema or codebase
multi_tenant_saas_readiness.path_to_60: Not achievable without the full tenant-isolation migration (Roadmap Stage 1) — this is the single largest, most foundational engineering effort identified in the entire audit
multi_tenant_saas_readiness.path_to_75: Tenant isolation plus self-serve signup, org creation, and email-based invites
multi_tenant_saas_readiness.path_to_90: Add billing/subscription/plan-entitlement layer, trial lifecycle, and per-tenant integration credentials

security_and_privacy.evidence: Zero accidental unauthenticated endpoints across 124 routes; parameterized SQL with an allowlist guard; correct OAuth CSRF (single-use random state nonce); zero hardcoded secrets in repo or git history; real, enforced AI cost controls. Confirmed gaps: OAuth tokens stored in plaintext, uneven audit-log coverage, no encryption at rest, no GDPR retention/export/erasure tooling.
security_and_privacy.strongest_aspect: Authentication/authorisation fundamentals — verified zero accidental gaps across every route in the backend
security_and_privacy.weakest_aspect: OAuth access/refresh tokens stored in plaintext with no encryption-at-rest layer anywhere in the codebase
security_and_privacy.path_to_60: Already at this level on fundamentals; encrypt OAuth tokens at rest to solidify it
security_and_privacy.path_to_75: Close audit-log coverage gaps (user lifecycle, outbound email actions); add GDPR retention/export/erasure tooling
security_and_privacy.path_to_90: Encryption at rest for the database itself; admin-impersonation/secure-support-access model; formal data-processing register

scalability_and_reliability.evidence: Solid migration strategy (31 sequential, append-only migrations); strong background-loop exception handling (two-layer, never dies from one bad cycle); confirmed zero observability/error-tracking anywhere; confirmed production DB grew ~29x in one month with no working automated backup; 22 unbounded list endpoints; 19 real missing indexes on FK-shaped columns.
scalability_and_reliability.strongest_aspect: Migration discipline and the background-job exception-handling pattern (two-layer, never permanently dies)
scalability_and_reliability.weakest_aspect: Confirmed active operational risk: no working automated database backup, combined with rapid, unexplained data growth
scalability_and_reliability.confidence_level: high on what was measured; the exact cause of DB growth is Inferred not Confirmed, blocked by this environment's own controls from a direct query
scalability_and_reliability.path_to_60: Install automated backups; diagnose and address the DB growth cause; add basic observability
scalability_and_reliability.path_to_75: Add pagination to unbounded endpoints; add the missing indexes
scalability_and_reliability.path_to_90: Multi-worker-safe rate limiting and background-job coordination if the deployment ever scales beyond one process

testing_and_maintainability.evidence: 40 backend tests pass, confirmed safely isolated (tmp-path DB per test file); zero frontend tests exist (no test runner configured in app/package.json); no lint/static-analysis tool configured for the frontend; tsc --noEmit is clean; zero TODO/FIXME/console.log leftovers found anywhere (genuinely clean hygiene); db.py is a single 2,760-line file holding the entire schema and every query function.
testing_and_maintainability.strongest_aspect: Backend test suite is real, safe, and passing (40/40); zero debug-leftover hygiene issues found anywhere in the codebase
testing_and_maintainability.weakest_aspect: Zero frontend tests and zero frontend lint/static-analysis tooling of any kind
testing_and_maintainability.path_to_60: Add a frontend test runner (even minimal smoke tests) and a lint config
testing_and_maintainability.path_to_75: Meaningful frontend test coverage on the core Leads/Pipeline/Outreach flows; backend coverage measurement
testing_and_maintainability.path_to_90: Split db.py's monolithic query functions into per-domain modules; CI-enforced coverage thresholds

inferred_findings.summary: The most plausible driver of the confirmed 29x database growth is the Companies House charge feed, which this repo's own project history documents as having recently started ingesting significantly more volume after a key-configuration bug was fixed.
inferred_findings.confidence: medium — plausible and consistent with existing project history, but not verified by a direct table-size query

inferred_findings.summary: Sequence-scheduler and activity-refresh background loops may be vulnerable to a duplicate-send on process crash between performing a side effect (e.g. sending a sequence email) and persisting updated state, unlike the CH stream which has confirmed strong idempotency.
inferred_findings.confidence: low-medium — plausible from the code structure, not exhaustively traced against exact ordering
